quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive using your four-way flashers.
Drive using your parking lights.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beam headlights when you are within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, which technique helps you avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.
Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
Engage the four-wheel drive on your vehicle.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow-covered or icy roads. Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless they are with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt normal traffic flow. You can receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive more slowly than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you may cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches you, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, sirens, or other warning devices approaches you, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, you must let pedestrians and other traffic that are still in the intersection pass through safely.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
Move to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to tell other drivers you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, you increase the risk of a crash. If you drive faster than surrounding traffic, you will need to pass many vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic at the legal speed limit. Pass only when needed.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A one-way street is starting.
A one-way street is ending.
A divided highway is starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead is a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When do you have the right-of-way to turn left?

options.text: When there is a solid green light.
When there is a flashing yellow light.
When there is a green arrow pointing left.
When there is a flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is a green arrow pointing left.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: ____ limit your focus, reaction time, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only high levels of alcohol can
Alcohol does not
Even small amounts of alcohol can
Only levels above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even small amounts of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol hurts your focus, reaction time, judgment, and memory. Your driving will suffer. Never drink and drive.

questions.question: If a worker is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the worker tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the worker says something different.
Assume the worker should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the worker tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a worker, sign, or police officer tells you to. Not following their directions is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit.
Stop.
Hospital.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop at red eight-sided signs.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly all the time.
Watches for what other drivers are doing.
Always drives at the same speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches for what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A good defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. It is against the law not to stop.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a stopped school bus loading or unloading children if:

options.text: You are traveling in the opposite direction on a two-way road with four or more lanes.
You are traveling in a rural area with wide shoulders on each side.
You are traveling in the same direction on a two-way road with four or more lanes.
The speed limit is under 25 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling in the opposite direction on a two-way road with four or more lanes.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, all traffic must stop while the school bus red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended. On a highway with two or more lanes in each direction, traffic coming from the opposite direction does not have to stop.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many types of drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is a criminal offense.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three

questions.correctAnswerText: All three
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating slows alcohol absorption slightly but cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive normally because their emotions will not affect their driving.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
Call a friend while driving to talk about their feelings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions distract you from driving. When worried, upset, angry, or crying, your mind is on something else, not the road. Calm yourself and get focused before you drive.

questions.question: An approaching driver does not dim their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Down the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an approaching driver does not dim their bright lights, look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded and lets you see the road well enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stay at the same speed.
Slow down so the other driver has room to pass safely and easily.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver has room to pass safely and easily.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough room in front of your vehicle to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be prepared to respond to yellow, red, or cross traffic.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
Make sure your tires are filled to the right pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, make sure your tires have good tread and are filled to the right pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react if something happens on the road. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not move until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When approaching a curve on a narrow road where you cannot see ahead clearly, it is best to:

options.text: Stop, get out, and walk around the curve to see what is ahead.
Flash your headlights on and off several times.
Honk your horn and stay close to the right edge of the road while driving slowly.
Speed up to get around the curve quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn and stay close to the right edge of the road while driving slowly.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see ahead on a narrow mountain road and are approaching a curve, honk your horn and drive slowly around the curve while staying close to the right edge of the road.

questions.question: When you hear the siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens go first, no matter which direction they are coming from. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing zones, no turns, and other driving rules.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press down on the wound to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can get back to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can see the road ahead clearly, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no traffic crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: U-turns are not allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Winding road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A sign with a red circle and red slash through the middle means something is not allowed. This sign means U-turns are not permitted in this location.
